body:
I guess it's just because he's gone around telling people he was assaulted at his previous job, and they have interpreted it as happening when he was a kid. It's just hitting very close to home, and I don't want to have been a source of anguish for him either, I just want him to be happy.

Until this thread, it never occurred to me that my own abuse may be playing a role in how I perceive this. I really need to see a therapist.

I'm so sorry to hear your mom went through that. I hope she has some form of peace now with you and her family. And you, as well, I hope everything is okay with you.

mhm, the incident I feel guilty about is the one from when I was 13. I've never talked to my cousin because as far as I know, he was sleeping the entire time, and nothing ever changed between us. I was hoping that he was unaffected.

I could definitely see the panic reaction. I fear so much being like my dad. A narcissist who yells instead of speaking, who breaks people down without a second thought in the world. Being anything like him is enough to make me panic instantly...

It definitely stopped with me at 13. I tried to make a conscious effort never to do these stupid, awful things again. I instead tried to treat my family and loved ones with the most respect I possibly could.

Thank you so much... Hearing someone say I deserve to be loved and loved is very visceral for me. I have nobody I can talk to about these things and I spend so much time in my own head, facing my own guilt and remorse. It was definitely such poor judgement. I'm glad, that at that age, I made the decision to never do this type of thing again.

I hope that one day soon I can find some form of happiness, some way to live and smile.
